chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Humran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a contracted slave who paid off part of his contract, then died, leaving a son from his slave girl. He said: If a condition was stipulated upon him, his son and his mother would become two slaves; and if no condition was stipulated upon him, his son would become free, pay the remainder of the contract to the masters, and the son would inherit what remained.

key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom in installments.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The contractual amount or price of manumission agreed upon by the slave.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the son of a deceased contracted slave if no condition was stipulated regarding his status?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the inheritance and manumission status of a mukatab's son based on the specific contractual stipulations made with the master, highlighting the principle that freedom is the default unless explicitly restricted. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on the autonomy of the mukatab's family unit and the equitable distribution of remaining assets, ensuring the son inherits what is left after settling the debt to the masters.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a contracted slave who had paid off some of his contractual amount, then died, and left a son of his from his slave girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there was a stipulated condition upon him, his son and his slave girl would become two slaves, and if there was no stipulated condition upon him, his son would become free and pay off to the master the remainder of the contract, and his son would inherit whatever remains’.
